operating_notes.text: Delhi GST authority withdrew the entire ₹55,20,45,266 input tax credit demand against Max Healthcare by Rectification Order dated 21 April 2026, closing the matter raised in the 30 December 2025 order.
Postal ballot closed 11 May 2026: 89.95% of outstanding shares polled on the re-appointment of Narayan K. Seshadri, 91.07% in favour and 8.93% against; public institutions voted 12.21% against.

Max Healthcare acquired ~58.28% of Kalinga Hospital Ltd., a 250-bed multi-specialty hospital in Bhubaneswar, for ~₹297.97 Cr, funded by a ₹300 Cr Senior Secured Term Loan in the form of External Commercial Borrowings.

BRS Capital Two Pte. Limited filed an oppression and mismanagement petition under sections 241 and 242 of the Companies Act before NCLT Cuttack against Kalinga Hospital Ltd. and Max Healthcare; orders on interim reliefs reserved, next heari
Board recommended final dividend of ₹2 per share for FY25-26.
Q4FY26 operational bed capacity was 4,966, up 412 beds in 12 months; 100-bed Bulandshahr hospital divested in Q2FY26.
International patient revenue was ₹227 Cr in Q4FY26, ~9% of hospital revenue, up 12% YoY.
Max Lab revenue ₹52 Cr (+14% YoY) and Max@Home ₹73 Cr (+30% YoY) in Q4FY26.
CCI orders dated 21 May 2026 closed the Section 4 abuse-of-dominance case over Delhi hospital pricing against 6 Max network hospitals with no adverse order.
FY26 network gross revenue was ₹10,538 Cr and net revenue ₹10,065 Cr, with operating EBITDA of ₹2,638 Cr (26.2% margin).
FY26 ARPOB was ₹78,000 versus ₹69,000 for Medanta, ₹48,000 for Apollo and ₹63,000 for Fortis.
Max Lab FY26 net revenue was ₹201 Cr (17% EBITDA margin) and Max@Home FY26 gross revenue ₹263 Cr.
Q4 FY26 network gross revenue stood at ₹2,664 Cr with ARPOB at ₹77,900 and occupancy over 75%.
Kalinga (Bhubaneswar) generated ₹154 Cr revenue in FY26 before acquisition; post-acquisition Q1FY27 occupancy was 50% and ARPOB ₹35,000.
Max Smart opened beds are running at 80% occupancy and Nanavati Phase 1 beds at about 80%; Nanavati Phase 2 will take about 2.5 years.
CGHS revenue is tracking the ₹140 Cr annual figure, with super-specialty rates flowing from June onwards.

timeline.summary: On 21 April 2026, Max Healthcare said the Delhi GST authority's Rectification Order dated the same day withdrew the entire ₹55.20 Cr input tax credit demand raised in its 30 December 2025 order.

On 12 May 2026, Max Healthcare reported that shareholders passed the postal ballot resolution re-appointing Mr. Narayan K. Seshadri as Non-Executive and Non-Independent Director with 91.07% of votes polled in favour.
On 13 May 2026, Max Healthcare announced receipt of a request from Radiant Life Care Hospital Foundation to re-classify from promoter group to public category following stake sale by promoters.
On 18 May 2026, Max Healthcare availed a ₹300 Cr ECB and completed the acquisition of ~58.28% of Kalinga Hospital Ltd. for ~₹297.97 Cr, making the 250-bed Bhubaneswar hospital a subsidiary.
BRS Capital Two filed an oppression and mismanagement petition before NCLT Cuttack against Kalinga Hospital Ltd. and Max Healthcare; NCLT reserved orders on interim reliefs.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹2,142.89 Cr (+12.2% YoY), net profit ₹342.22 Cr (+7.3% YoY).

On 22 May 2026, Max Healthcare said the CCI, by orders dated 21 May 2026, held no case of abuse of dominant position under Section 4 against its network hospitals and closed the matter with no adverse order.
Max Healthcare Institute Limited’s **Dhiraj Aroraa (SVP - Company Secretary and Compliance Officer)** posted earnings call recording on May 22, 2026, for Q4FY26 and FY26 results.
Max Healthcare Institute Limited filed its investor presentation for the UBS Asian Investment Conference 2026 detailing FY26 financial and operational highlights.
Max Healthcare reported Q4 FY26 revenue of ₹2,664 Cr (+10% YoY) and PAT of ₹387 Cr, and announced a ₹1,400 Cr greenfield hospital in Lucknow.
Abhay Soi and Aditya Soi declared no encumbrance on Max Healthcare shares under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) for FY2025-26.
Max Healthcare announced postal ballot voting results on October 19, 2026, approving RSU schemes, CMD remuneration, and MoA alteration.
